title: Cloud channel marketplace sync — prep notes (Ryan)
body:
Context / why this sync: quick prep for 1:1 with cloud marketplace ops leads (AWS, GCP, Azure) + channel partner manager. Goal is to unblock listing certification, align on billing/procurement expectations, and surface any technical blockers for private/dedicated deployment options.

Meeting goals (top 3):
- Clarity on timelines for marketplace promotions (AWS feature drop window, GCP listing verification, Azure certification SLA).
- Agree on required artifacts from Redwood (SaaS onboarding doc, security attestation, sample SLA language).
- Identify owners & deadlines for each marketplace path so we can commit to dates for customer enablement.

Attendees to confirm (ask Aisha to confirm):
- AWS ops: Maya (onboarding), Tobias (payments)
- GCP: Lina (partner listings)
- Azure: Matt (certification)
- Channel PM: Jordan L.
- Me (Ryan) + Aisha (GTM)

Draft agenda (30–40m total):
1) Quick intros + success metric we care about (2m)
2) Where each marketplace is vs. our checklist (5–7m) — current blockers (technical/legal/billing)
3) Technical clarifications (10m) — private listing vs public, marketplace-proxied billing for Dedicated, container image vs AMI recommendation
4) GTM / co-marketing asks (5m) — featured listing, joint webinar window (target Apr-May), joint case study process
5) Action items and owners (5–10m)
6) Parking lot / follow-up cadence (2m)

Prep notes for each marketplace:
- AWS Marketplace:
  - Status: onboarding convo last week; listing in draft but need Marketplace Entitlement Service (MES) integration details.
  - Tech ask: which deployment artifact do they recommend for Redwood Dedicated + Private? AWS team prefers AMI for on-prem but will accept container images for EKS listing. Ask: confirm if MES supports our token-based usage metering (we bill per-token).
  - Legal/billing: need procurement flow doc (how a customer is invoiced via AWS vs direct Redwood). Outline what we currently offer: hosted API usage-billing (direct), Dedicated reserved capacity (contract), Private (license + infra).
  - Risk: MES metering granularity — might require mapping tokens -> usage units; ask eng to estimate integration lift.

- GCP Marketplace:
  - Status: listing intake form submitted; partner team flagged data residency language for private deployments.
  - Tech ask: GCP prefers container registry + deployment script. Confirm whether on-prem offering needs additional packaging.
  - Certification: security questionnaire outstanding (SOC2 snippets + KMS integration notes). Priya to surface latest SOC2 artifact.
  - Commercial: GCP's trial credits and promo windows — align for co-marketing push in May.

- Azure Marketplace:
  - Status: certification portal still shows 'in review' for our app registration. Matt indicated a doc gap on key rotation policy.
  - Tech ask: Marketplace billing for metered instances — verify they can support per-token or whether we need to translate into host-hour equivalents.
  - Legal: Azure has stricter procurement terms in EU; coordinate with legal on clause for data processing addendum (DPA).

Channel partner items (cross-marketplace):
- Channel PM wants a single one-pager that maps Redwood product modes to marketplace artifacts (Hosted API -> listing type A, Dedicated -> listing type B, Private -> partner referral flow). Draft one-pager today.
- Need to confirm marketing assets: logo pack, 1-pager, 1 technical whitepaper (2 pager) and 1 quickstart for customers.

Open technical questions for SRE/serving-runtime (Ryan to take offline w/ eng):
- How feasible is providing an 'agent image' (container) that marketplace teams can deploy directly? Rough ETA for engineering: target estimate by Fri 2026-03-05.
- Token metering shim: can we emit usage events to MES / GCP billing endpoints? If not, what's the mapping strategy? (Ask eng for FTE estimate).
- KV cache persistence for private deployments: doc gap for marketplaces — need short doc explaining cache behavior and VPN / VPC networking requirements.

Immediate action items (short list, put dates):
- Ryan: draft the marketplace artifact mapping one-pager + attach current pricing matrix (due 2026-03-03).
- Aisha: confirm webinar window with marketing and draft co-marketing ask (due 2026-03-06).
- Priya: upload latest SOC2 / security snippets to Confluence and share link (due 2026-03-02).
- Jordan L.: ask AWS ops for MES sample payloads + whether they support custom meters (due 2026-03-04).
- Eng owner (TBD): feasibility estimate for token metering integration (due 2026-03-05).

Notes to self / talking points:
- Emphasize we don't need identical billing semantics across marketplaces — we can translate tokens -> invoiceable units as long as it's transparent and measurable.
- Push for at least one 'public listing' per cloud as a beachhead; private marketplace paths can be second phase.
- Use Dedicated offering as the main enterprise anchor on the marketplaces (predictable throughput + SLA = easier procurement story).

Parking lot / future asks (not for this meeting unless raised):
- Explore marketplace partner referral credits for resellers.
- Sync with Solutions Engineering to create a Marketplace deployment runbook (templated ARM/CloudFormation + k8s helm).
- Investigate partnership with a managed service partner (for on-prem installs).

Follow-up cadence: propose weekly 30m triage for next 6 weeks to unblock certifications; then biweekly. Ask each marketplace to nominate a weekly contact.

Misc. links to include in meeting invite: Confluence onboarding page, current pricing matrix (sheet), sample SLA draft (doc), Slack thread link. Add these when sending invite.

Scratch / rough shorthand:
- "MES tokens" = AWS Marketplace Entitlement Service mapping question
- "meter-shim" = small service to convert per-token to marketplace meter units
- customer flow: marketplace purchase -> marketplace billing -> entitlement -> Redwood routing -> Dedicated/private exchange

End of prep. Will update after 1:1 and paste action items back into this doc.
